scope: Doorkeeper01–03 exact-original review for continuity, distinct assigned-work/watch/household actions, anatomy, contact and Mark13:34–37 source boundaries.
globalConditions: Technical review is not owner approval or final browser acceptance.
Unnamed figures illustrate Jesus' comparison; pictured specific tasks are artistic choices.

entries.alt: A bald, gray-bearded householder speaks with open hands to a young man and two other household workers standing at the doorway with linen and a basket.
entries.caption: Jesus compares watchfulness to a man leaving his house and giving each servant work to do. He also commands the doorkeeper to keep watch.
entries.findings: Distinct bald gray-bearded master/olive wrap, young dark-curled clean-shaven doorkeeper/light tunic/black sash, gray-curled bearded worker/brown and woman/rust headcloth. Listener attention and master palms credible; folded hands, linen hold and basket support coherent. Natural skin, textiles and doorway materials.
conditions: Objects illustrate household work; Mark does not specify linen handling or carrying baskets.
No precise household size, biography or narrated departure ceremony is established.

entries.alt: The young doorkeeper rests a hand on the open wooden door and looks out into a darkening lane, with an oil lamp burning on a shelf beside him.
entries.caption: The doorkeeper watches because the time of the master's return is unknown. The open doorway pictures readiness, without showing that the master has arrived.
entries.findings: Young face, curls, tunic and black sash match01. Hand contacts door coherently, hanging hand natural; outward gaze appropriate to watch rather than absent interpersonal contact. Shelf lamp rests physically on stone with flame away from nearby cloth; night lighting photographic.
conditions: No visitor or returning master is visible; do not infer arrival from his outward gaze.
Exact time of night, lamp and open-door arrangement are illustrative.

entries.alt: A woman folds linen at a table, a gray-haired man handles a large jar on a shelf, and the young doorkeeper looks out through the open doorway.
entries.caption: The household's work continues while the doorkeeper remains attentive. Folding linen and tending stored vessels illustrate the work entrusted to each servant as Jesus calls all His listeners to watch.
entries.findings: Allthree workers retain01 faces, clothing and roles; doorkeeper also matches02. Cloth grips, jar contact with both hands, shelf support, door palm and standing anatomy plausible. Task-directed gazes fit respective work. Lamps on table and hanging support physically credible; natural photographic texture. Distinct broader household action rather than repeating solitary watch only.
conditions: Linen folding and vessel handling are imagined examples, not tasks specifically named by Mark.
No promise of reward, completed arrival or exact length of waiting is shown.
Lamp placement is an illustrative scene, not a claim of a certified safe household arrangement.
